openings.claim: Inherited allocations and missing compatibility information may cause exclusion; needs-based reassignment could improve access.
openings.discriminator: Compare both schedules against identical stated demand: improvement supports allocation effects; infeasible compatible demand indicates restricted-time or piano capacity limits despite 68% reservation utilization.
openings.probe: Converse with contacts by telephone or in person about total weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum usable duration, including needs rehearsed elsewhere. Construct an eight-week paper schedule locking performances and weekly guarantees, then allocate additional time; obtain group agreement before changes.
openings.uncertainty: Needs and alternatives are unrecorded; blank equipment entries do not imply flexibility. Contact reliability and feasibility are unproven; 60 minutes cannot satisfy a longer need automatically.

openings.claim: An authoritative ledger with numbered bookings, explicit change supersession and verbal readback may reduce conflicting expectations and reconciliation.
openings.discriminator: Fewer divergent records supports record consistency; conflicts despite matching current confirmations implicate communication or interpretation. Added recording overhead may exceed savings.
openings.probe: Update the desk ledger before confirmation; read back room/date/time, mark online-copy update time, and track confirmation identifiers, conflict circumstances and all administration minutes across eight weeks, alongside needs fulfillment.
openings.uncertainty: Consistent volunteer/desk use is assumed. Record inconsistency explains only some conflicts; staffing feasibility remains unproven.

lineage.reason: Retains compatibility hypothesis and capacity discriminator.
Adds allocation order and duration safeguard.

decision: Probe both hypotheses; neither dominates established evidence. Preserve two rooms, existing equipment, 24 staffed hours/week, no fees, both dated performances, requested weekly 60-minute access within available opening periods, and telephone/in-person changes without accounts. Eight-week targets: at least 90% stated needs within acceptable windows, fewer than two conflicts, administration averaging at most 120 minutes/week. Baseline: three conflicts, 127.5 minutes/week; fulfillment denominator unknown. Synthetic observations leave actual occupancy, membership overlap and missed-session causes/recoverability unmeasured.
